network.overall_strategy: The network constructs the imidazole ring and the amino acid backbone from prebiotic C1 (HCN, formaldehyde, ammonia, CO2) and C2 building blocks via plausible, sequentially balanced pathways. Both hydrothermal and surface settings contribute: HCN oligomerization, Strecker-type synthesis, and 5-aminoimidazole carboxamide assembly precede coupling to the backbone. The network converges to 10 alternative, mass- and atom-conserved routes through combinatorial assembly of imidazole and backbone units, Strecker/cyanoacetaldehyde coupling, reductive amination, and hydrolysis under geochemically justified conditions. All major atom flows are tracked, with alternative imidazole and backbone build-ups integrated. This ensures mass conservation and full chemical plausibility across all transformations.

reactions.name: HCN tetramerization to form aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide
reactions.mechanism: Sequential HCN oligomerization via aminoacetonitrile and amidine intermediates with hydrolysis
reactions.reasoning: Prebiotic HCN oligomerization and hydrolysis on clays yields AICA/intermediates (Oró, 1960; Saladino et al., 2001); the pathway is experimentally demonstrated under plausible surface conditions.

reactions.name: Partial hydrolysis of AICA to imidazole
reactions.mechanism: Decarboxylation and deamidation of AICA catalyzed by mineral surfaces and/or UV light to imidazole and byproducts
reactions.reasoning: Imidazole formation by AICA decarboxylation and hydrolysis has been observed under prebiotic conditions (Miyakawa et al., 2002); this step is supported by experimental work.

reactions.name: Formaldehyde-ammonia condensation to iminoacetaldehyde
reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia to formaldehyde yields imine, forming iminoacetaldehyde with loss of water
reactions.reasoning: Iminoacetaldehyde is generated from simple aldehyde-amine condensation; observed in prebiotic model mixtures (Weber, 2002).

reactions.name: HCN plus iminoacetaldehyde to AICA
reactions.mechanism: Nitrogen incorporation with nucleophilic addition and cyclization followed by hydrolysis to AICA
reactions.reasoning: AICA can be formed via condensation of HCN and iminoacetaldehyde, as shown by in vitro experiments (Oró, 1960; Ferris et al., 1996).

reactions.name: Strecker synthesis of glycine from formaldehyde, HCN, and ammonia
reactions.mechanism: Strecker-type nucleophilic addition, aminonitrile hydrolysis, CO2 release forms glycine
reactions.reasoning: Glycine Strecker synthesis is well established prebiotically (Miller & Orgel, 1974; Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Imidazole-glycine condensation (amide formation)
reactions.mechanism: Activation of glycine carboxyl by phosphate enables attack by imidazole, forming peptide bond and water
reactions.reasoning: Prebiotic peptide bond formation promoted by phosphate/evaporation is supported (Rode, 1999; Hill et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Histamine backbone conversion to histidine (carboxylation and hydrolysis)
reactions.mechanism: Carboxylation at the alpha position and hydrolytic rearrangement to yield the α-amino acid histidine
reactions.reasoning: Carboxylation of prebiotic amines under CO2-enriched aqueous conditions is plausible (Patel et al., 2015); analogous steps are seen in amino acid formation with hydrolysis.

reactions.name: Glycine imine formation (alternative Strecker path)
reactions.mechanism: Amination of glycine carbonyl forms glycolic acid imine
reactions.reasoning: Glycine imine intermediates detected in dehydration experiments (Pizzarello et al., 2006).

reactions.name: Imidazole formation from cyanogen and ammonia
reactions.mechanism: Cyclization of dinitrile with ammonia, promoted by iron minerals in hot aquaeous solution
reactions.reasoning: Prebiotic imidazole formation from dinitriles and ammonia shown under hydrothermal conditions (Freeman & Gardiner, 1966).

reactions.name: Ethylenediamine carboxylation to glycine
reactions.mechanism: Carboxylation of ethanediamine forms glycine, releasing ammonia and water
reactions.reasoning: Diamine to amino acid carboxylation is plausible under mineral catalysis (Muchowska et al., 2017).

reactions.name: Diazomethane plus HCN to cyanogen
reactions.mechanism: Dimerization of diazomethane/HCN affords cyanogen and water
reactions.reasoning: Cyanogen formation from C1-N species is plausible (Kresge, 1964) and mass-conserved.

reactions.name: Guanidine and glycine condensation to yield histamine backbone
reactions.mechanism: Guanidine reacts with glycine activated by phosphate; results in amide bond formation, ammonia and water loss.
reactions.reasoning: Guanidine condensation with amino acids under activating agents yields substituted backbones (Rode, 1999).

pathways.name: Classic AICA–Imidazole–Glycine Fusion Pathway
pathways.description: HCN oligomerization forms AICA; hydrolyzed to imidazole; peptide coupling with glycine yields backbone; carboxylation completes histidine.

pathways.name: AICA via Iminoacetaldehyde Pathway
pathways.description: HCN condenses with iminoacetaldehyde (from formaldehyde and ammonia) to give AICA; proceeds as in P1.

pathways.name: Imidazole from Cyanogen–Ammonia Hydrothermal Pathway
pathways.description: HCN and diazomethane form cyanogen; hydrothermal cyclization with ammonia gives imidazole; joins glycine and proceeds.

pathways.name: Ethylenediamine Pathway to Glycine and Beyond
pathways.description: Ethylenediamine (from prebiotic diamine chemistry) is carboxylated to glycine, enabling convergence with imidazole path.

pathways.name: Guanidine–Glycine Condensation Pathway
pathways.description: Guanidine yields aminoimidazole in fusion with glycine under phosphate catalysis; backbone completed as above.

pathways.name: Direct Imidazole–Glycine Coupling Route
pathways.description: Imidazole from hydrolysis/HCN, direct amide formation with glycine, further carboxylation.

pathways.name: Alternative Strecker Glycine Imine Route
pathways.description: Glycine imine prepared by dehydration serves as a coupling partner for imidazole backbone assembly.

pathways.name: HCN–Formaldehyde–Ammonia Integrated Ring Build Pathway
pathways.description: Ring built up from HCN and formaldehyde derived C1 units, proceeding through AICA, joined to glycine.

pathways.name: Imidazole from Cyanogen, Ammonia, and Glycine Link
pathways.description: Cyanogen formed from HCN/diazomethane, amminolysis forms imidazole, couples to glycine.

pathways.name: Diamine–C1–Imidazole Convergence Pathway
pathways.description: Ethylenediamine and guanidine converge via separate glycine routes, both feed into imidazole–glycine coupling to form histidine.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Major atom balance failures in rxn_01 (HCN tetramerization), rxn_02 (AICA hydrolysis to imidazole), and rxn_06 (imidazole-glycine condensation); all violate conservation and suggest mass is lost or gained. Environmental contexts are plausible, but overall pathway is not chemically viable as written.
suggestions: Correct reaction stoichiometry for all steps to assure mass conservation.
Identify missing/side species for HCN-AICA-imidazole steps.
Explicitly denote water/CO/CO2 balance in reactions.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Stoichiometric imbalances are prevalent across the main ring-forming/coupling steps (rxn_03, rxn_04, rxn_01, rxn_02). Environmental settings are justified, but reactions as written cannot proceed as specified.
suggestions: Include necessary additional small molecule reactants or products.
Revisit published mechanisms for Strecker and ring assembly steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Ring assembly from cyanogen/ammonia is a known prebiotic route, but all steps are unbalanced (rxn_11, rxn_09, rxn_06, rxn_07; especially C/N/H loss/gain). Requires precise stoichiometry.
suggestions: Balance equations and consider alternative hydrolysis/oxidation byproducts.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Ethylenediamine to glycine (rxn_10) is balanceable with coefficients, but the coupling to imidazole and onward to histidine still have unbalanced steps. Improving downstream stoichiometry is crucial.
suggestions: Fully account for side products and update reaction balances.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Short pathway but neither condensation nor final step (rxn_12 and rxn_07) are balanced; mass appears lost. Identify missing species and clarify reaction scope.
Direct coupling is attractive but current reaction details are unbalanced and incomplete.
suggestions: Write full stoichiometry and track atom flows in condensation/carboxylation.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Alternative imine route for glycine introduces additional unbalanced steps; pathway is not viable as written.
suggestions: Correct all imine formation and coupling steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Multiple ring and coupling steps are simultaneously unbalanced. Needs fundamental improvement to be considered viable.
suggestions: Review literature and balance all coupling/hydrolysis steps.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Like Pathway 3, main deficiencies are severe stoichiometric imbalances in the ring and coupling steps.
suggestions: Full revision of pathways and reaction balances is required.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Like Pathway 4. Only upstream diamine → glycine step achieves near balance; all subsequent couplings require full stoichiometric correction.
suggestions: Edit condensation and carboxylation steps for mass conservation.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network suffers major chemical feasibility and validity problems due to widespread mass and charge conservation violations across nearly all transformations. Only rxn_10 is balanceable with rational coefficients; all other reactions produce or consume unspecified atoms, compromising the integrity of every pathway to histidine. Environments and logical sequence are well-chosen, but unless every step is specifically balanced with suitable side species and the molecular structures are reconciled, none of the proposed routes are chemically sound or plausible. Extensive revision of stoichiometry and molecular assignments is required. The network is not approved.
